summary.detail: Selected follow-up Master's programmes (two years). English-language track open to all eligible countries: about 126 programmes at 18 Czech universities in the official 2026 list (engineering, natural sciences, business and law, ICT, agriculture, economics and political science, among others). Czech-language track only for citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Ukraine and Belarus (democratic forces): one-year Czech language course at Charles University's Institute for Language and Preparatory Studies, funded by the scholarship, then selected areas of study (economics, international relations and political science, journalism, finance and insurance, management and administration, natural sciences, ICT, engineering, agriculture and veterinary).

Lists are for the 2027/2028 call (applications 21 Aug - 30 Sep 2026), now closed. The spreadsheets contain a few placeholder codes (e.g. 'TBS') for programmes not yet accredited.
Completed bachelor's / master's are entry requirements, not funded levels.

summary.detail: Master's Degree programmes (Laurea Magistrale, 2nd cycle) at public or legally recognised Italian institutions, attended in person; 9-month scholarship period, potentially renewable. No field restriction or programme list in the call (any discipline). Italian- or English-taught programmes (B2 in the language of instruction). AFAM (Higher Education for Fine Arts, Music and Dance) programmes, 1st and 2nd cycle, are also funded for 9 months, potentially renewable.

PhD programmes in Italy, 9-month scholarship period, potentially renewable; applicant must hold the admission letter to the PhD programme. Research projects under academic supervision (including co-tutorships) are funded separately for 9 months, not renewable, at universities, public research institutions, recognised museums and archives. Any discipline; no programme list.
summary.source_text: Scholarships for PhD programmes are awarded for a period of study of 9 (nine) months and are potentially renewable.

notes: Source is the full English call text for 2026-2027 (Bando-26-27-ENG.pdf, 13 pages) hosted on the Italian Embassy in Abidjan site (MAECI network), plus the Panama embassy notice. The call could not be fetched from esteri.it or studyinitaly.esteri.it (bot check; ListaBandi still shows only the 2025-26 call as closed). Deadline 26 March 2026; no 2027-28 call published.

Bachelor's (Laurea triennale) and single-cycle degrees are covered only as renewals of 'Costruiamo il futuro' scholarships awarded under the 2025-26 call (art. 1.6), so bachelor is not an open level. AFAM 1st cycle is also covered but the call does not call it bachelor.
Research projects: call states no level (age limit 40, supervisor invitation letter); not coded as postdoctoral.
Also offered: 3-month 'Italofonia' Italian language and culture courses (A2 required), not a degree level.

summary.detail: Full-time bachelor's programmes at participating Dutch institutions (11 research universities and 23 universities of applied sciences/arts listed for 2026-2027). EUR 5,000 paid in the first year, not a full-tuition scholarship. No general field restriction on the Study in NL page; eligible programmes and fields are set by each institution on its own scholarship page.
summary.source_text: You are applying for a full-time bachelor’s or master’s programme at one of the participating Dutch higher education institutions.

summary.detail: Full-time master's programmes at the same participating institutions (research universities: Eindhoven University of Technology, Maastricht University, Radboud University, University of Groningen, University of Twente, Utrecht University, VU Amsterdam, Wageningen University & Research and others). Eligible programmes are defined per institution.
summary.source_text: You are applying for a full-time bachelor’s or master’s programme at one of the participating Dutch higher education institutions.

notes: The page does not list programmes; it links to each participating institution's NL Scholarship page and says to check the institution's website for the fields of study for this academic year. The participating list changes every year.
Requirements on page: non-EEA nationality; no degree from an education institution in the Netherlands. Formerly known as Holland Scholarship.

summary.detail: Research stay of 1 to 9 months at an Austrian university for postgraduates pursuing a doctoral/PhD programme outside Austria. All disciplines. Age limit 35. The Austrian supervisor must confirm the project can be carried out in English; all Austrian universities are eligible hosts (non-university research institutes case by case). Stays are for academic year 2027/28, full calendar months only.
summary.source_text: Postgraduates pursuing a doctoral/PhD programme outside Austria

summary.detail: Research stay of 1 to 9 months at an Austrian university for postgraduates and post-docs who finished their studies at a non-Austrian university after 30 September 2025, and for post-docs working as lecturers or researchers at a university outside Austria. All disciplines.
summary.source_text: Post-docs who are working as lecturers or researchers at a university outside Austria

notes: Main page: 'young researchers from all disciplines and countries (except Austria)', duration '1 to 9 months'. Funds a research stay, not a degree programme, so there are no programmes to list.
Current Austrian university students and people permanently resident in Austria are excluded.
Other Ernst Mach strands (FH, Follow-Up, ASEA-UNINET) are separate programmes.

summary.detail: Full-time, one- or two-year English-taught master's studies at Swedish universities within four study fields: Governance, Public Health, Entrepreneurship and Innovation, and STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics). Only master's programmes on SI's eligible list qualify; the 2027/2028 list is due on the page on 13 November 2026. Stockholm School of Economics and Konstfack applicants go through separate intakes.
summary.source_text: The scholarship supports full-time, one- or two-year master’s studies at Swedish universities

notes: The list of eligible master's programmes for 2027/2028 is published on 13 November 2026; as of 2026-10-23 no programmes can be named, hence partly. Programmes are applied for via University Admissions (admission is a precondition).
Page fetched via curl (WebFetch returned 403). Open to citizens of 34 listed countries; page says information may be subject to changes.
